push/pushes: A grader gives four sampled answers rewards of zero point nine, zero point six, zero point five and zero point two. Used as they are, every one pushes its answer up.
push/flip: Subtract a baseline, b, of zero point five five, and each push uses the advantage, A, equal to R minus b. Now the last two push down.
push/worry: So every single step changes. Does training still climb J, the expected reward, on average, or has b steered it somewhere else?
push/one: It still climbs J, because a model's probabilities must always add up to one.
one/bars: Take the seven times eight model: fifty six half the time, fifty four three times in ten, and sixty four twice. Laid end to end, they fill exactly one.
one/nudge: Raise theta zero, the score of fifty six. Its share grows, so the other two must shrink: together they still make one.
one/slopes: Measure it as the log trick did, with a nudge of zero point zero one. Fifty six gains zero point zero zero two five: a slope, partial pi, partial theta zero, of zero point two five.
one/others: The other two give that back: their slopes are minus zero point one five and minus zero point one.
one/zero: Add the three, and you get zero. Whatever one probability gains, the others lose.
one/always: That holds for any parameter and any number of answers. Know all the slopes but one, and the last is minus the sum of the rest.
cancel/dlog: The policy gradient uses slopes of ln pi, though: by the log trick, the slope of pi divided by pi. For fifty six, zero point two five over zero point five is zero point five.
cancel/rest: Fifty four and sixty four both come out at minus zero point five.
cancel/part: Subtracting b takes b times that slope off the estimate for whichever answer was drawn: plus zero point five times b for fifty six, and minus zero point five times b for the others.
cancel/avg: Average over the model's draws. Fifty six turns up half the time, bringing plus zero point five times b; the other two make up the other half, bringing minus zero point five times b. They cancel.
cancel/why: That is no accident. Weighting by probability undoes the division: pi times the slope of ln pi is just the slope of pi. And those always add up to zero.
cancel/E: An average over the model's draws is written with a double-struck E, E, for expected value. With b or without, the expected estimate is the same.
cancel/noise: What b does change is each single estimate: good answers are pushed up and poor ones down, so the estimates swing less.
cancel/williams: Ronald Williams proved this in 1992, for any baseline that does not depend on the answer drawn.
cancel/name: He built the baseline into the name. REINFORCE stands for reward increment equals nonnegative factor, times offset reinforcement, times characteristic eligibility.
cancel/map: That is the step itself: a step size, times R minus b, times the slope of ln pi of the answer drawn.
try/p1: Try one. Three answers have probabilities zero point five, zero point three and zero point two. For a parameter theta zero, partial ln pi, partial theta zero is zero point four for answer zero, and minus one for answer one. What is it for answer two?
try/a1: Weighted by probability, the three must add up to zero. The first two bring zero point two and minus zero point three: together, minus zero point one.
try/a2: So answer two must bring plus zero point one. Divide by its probability: zero point one over zero point two is zero point five.
